contenido: Canon 1 Let not the faith of the three hundred and eighteen Fathers who met at Nicaea in Bithynia be violated, but let it remain firm; and let all heresy be anathematized, and especially the heresy of those who contradict the faith, namely, of the Eunomians or Anomeans, and of the Arians or Eudoxians, and of the Semi-Arians or Pneumatomachans, and of the Sabellians, and of the Marcellians, and of the Photinians, and of the Apollinarians.

Canon 2 Bishops who are over a diocese do not approach the Churches beyond their limits, nor confuse the Churches; but that, according to the canons, the bishop of Alexandria administers only what is in Egypt; and the bishops of the East govern only the East, preserving the privileges that the Nicene canons attribute to the Church of Antioch; and the bishops of the diocese of Asia administer only what is in Asia; and those of Pontus only what is in Pontus; and those of Thrace what is in Thrace. Unassigned bishops do not approach, beyond the diocese, any ordinations or other ecclesiastical administrations, unless they are called. Having observed the said rule regarding the dioceses, it is clear that what belongs to each province is administered by the provincial synod, as established by the Nicene decree. And it is appropriate that the Churches of God that exist among barbarian nations be administered according to the custom they obtained from the Fathers.
Canon 3 It is appropriate that the bishop of the city of Constantinople have the primacies of honor after the bishop of Rome, because it is the new Rome.

Canon 4 About Maximus the Cynic and his disorderly ordination in Constantinople: so that Maximus neither was nor is a bishop, nor are those who were ordained by him, in any degree of the clergy, and that everything that was done around him or by him is void.

Canon 5 Concerning the volume of the Westerners, we also receive those who in Antioch confess a single Deity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

Canon 6 Since many, confusing the ecclesiastical and lay order, feign enmity and slander against the orthodox bishops, desiring nothing more than to tarnish the reputation of priests and excite tumults among peaceful peoples: it has seemed to the holy synod not to admit accusers without examination, nor to allow everyone to utter accusations against the rectors of the Church, nor to exclude everyone. But if anyone presents any complaint of his own, that is, private, against the bishop, such as for fraud or other injury: in such accusations neither the person of the accuser nor the religion is examined. Well, it is appropriate that the conscience of the bishop be free, and that the one who claims to have been injured, of whatever religion he may be, obtains justice. If, however, it were an ecclesiastical accusation against the bishop, then the examination of the persons must be made: so that, in the first place, it is not lawful for heretics to accuse orthodox bishops of ecclesiastical crimes. We call heretics both those who have long since abdicated from the Church, and those whom we later anathematize; and in addition to these, also those who confess to the Orthodox faith, but have made a schism and gather congregations against our canonical bishops. Therefore, also if some have been condemned in ecclesiastical causes or excommunicated, either from the clergy or from the lay order, it is not lawful for them to accuse the bishop before they first make their own accusation. Likewise, those who are under prejudice of accusations should not be allowed to accuse the bishop before they show themselves innocent of the crimes with which they are linked. If some, without being heretics, nor excommunicated, nor condemned, nor accused of some crimes, said they had some ecclesiastical accusation against the bishop: the holy synod orders these to first present the accusations before the provincial bishops and before them to argue the guilty of the crimes. If it should happen that the provincial bishops fail in the trial regarding the bishop's crimes, then they should go to the greatest synod of bishops of that diocese, and present the accusation before them, first promising in writing to submit to the trial if they are convicted of slanderers. If anyone, despising this, dares to disturb the royal ears, or the judgments of secular princes, or the ecumenical synod, despising the entire order of the provincial bishops: this one must in no way be admitted to the accusation, as one who has made the canons despised and has confused the ecclesiastical order.

Canon 7 Those who come from heresy to the orthodox faith and the part of those who are saved, we receive according to the following order and custom. We receive the Arians, and the Macedonians, and the Sabbatins, and the Novatians, who are called Cathars and Aristeros, and the Tetradites or Quartodecimans, and the Apollinarians, giving libels and anathematizing every heresy that does not feel like the holy Catholic and Apostolic Church of God, signed, that is, anointed first with the holy chrism on the forehead and in the eyes and in noses and in the mouth and in the ears, and when we sign them we say: "Seal of the gift of the Holy Spirit." But the Eunomians, who are baptized in a single immersion, and the Montanists, who here are called Phrygians, and the Sabellians, who teach the Son-Father and do some other serious things, and all the other heresies (for there are many here, especially those who come from the region of the Galatians), all of these who want to approach orthodoxy we receive as Gentiles. And the first day we make them Christians, the second catechumens, then the third day we exorcise them, with triple blows in the face and in the ears; and so we catechize them, and make them remain in the Church for a long time and hear the Scriptures, and then we baptize them.
